🇬🇧 At PMQs this week, Andy Burnham said national security "can't come at the expense of social security."

It's meant to sound compassionate. It's actually the most dangerous inversion in politics — and it deserves taking apart.

National security isn't one priority among many. It's the FOUNDATION the others stand on. The pension, the NHS, universal credit — every pound of social security only exists because there's a secure, functioning country to provide it in. Remove the security and there's nothing left to hand out. You can't pay a pension in a country that can't defend its borders. Ask Ukraine whether national security can wait.

And let's be honest about why he said it. The same week, his Chancellor John Healey — who RESIGNED as Defence Secretary in June over defence funding — confirmed he'll shelve the 3%-by-2030 target in next month's Budget. "It can't come at the expense of social security" is the slogan that dresses that climbdown up as a moral choice instead of a broken promise.

To be fair: nobody wants vulnerable people abandoned. But that's not the real choice. A serious country that cut Whitehall waste and controlled its borders could fund BOTH a proper defence and a decent safety net. "The tank or the food bank" is a confession of failure dressed up as a value.

Reform UK: national security first — because without it there is nothing to protect anyone with. Defending the country and looking after its people are not opposites. They're the same duty.
